newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau police swoop on illegal gambling den.
newsitem.headline: Macau police swoop on illegal gambling den.

text.p: Macau police said on Friday they had broken up an illegal betting operation being run from flat in the Portuguese-run enclave and arrested a Hong Kong man.

Acting on a tip from Hong Kong's anti-graft body, the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC), Macau police seized several computers and 10 telephone sets at the flat, a source close to investigations told Reuters.
Notebooks containing a long list of names and Hong Kong telephone numbers were found, the source said.
The arrested man is believed to have been running the operation in Macau as a bookmaking centre for a racket based in neighbouring Hong Kong, a police source told Reuters.
"They (illegal bookmakers in Hong Kong) set up shop in Macau because they think that it's safe for them here, far away from the ICAC in Hong Kong," the source said.
Hong Kong was shaken this week by a horse race fixing and illegal betting scandal that has implicated almost 40 people, including trainers and jockeys.
The ICAC has charged five people, including two Malaysian citizens, with illegal bookmaking.
